newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet Ramsey's parents deny role in her murder.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet Ramsey's parents deny role in her murder.

text.p: The parents of JonBenet Ramsey on Thursday denied they murdered their daughter and pledged to track down the killer of the 6-year-old beauty pageant winner.

At a secretly-arranged news conference with select members of the local media, John and Patricia Ramsey, seated side by side, also said that rumours their daughter was sexually molested were "totaly false."
"I did not kill my daughter JonBenet," John Ramsey said. "I will miss her dearly for the rest of my life."

The girl's body was found on Dec. 26 by her father in the basement of the family's home, about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000. No arrests have been made and no suspects named.

The Ramseys have been targets of the investigation amid widespread speculation they may have played a role in the murder. Until Wednesday, when they answered questions from the police, they had declined to be formally interviewed by investigators.
Patricia Ramsey, her voice cracking, denied murdering her daughter and said she would not rest until police found the real killer.
"I did not kill JonBenet," she said. "I did not have anything to do with it. I loved that child with my whole heart and soul."
Looking straight into the camera, Patricia Ramsey addressed the killer, saying: "You may be eluding the authorities at this time, but God knows who you are and we will find you."

The couple also denied there was anything improper in the beauty pageants their daughter took part in where she was often dressed up to look older, saying the contests were only a small part of the child's life.

According to reports, seven journalists were invited to meet with the Ramseys at a hotel in Boulder. The reporters were told to be in Boulder about 10 a.m. on Thursday and were then called on their cellular phones and advised of the location of the secret meeting. Several video cameramen and still photographers also were permitted to attend the news conference and the footage was later made to local TV stations and aired on CNN.

Other reporters were excluded from the press conference. The journalists had to agree not to ask any questions about police interviews of the couple on Wednesday nor about the day that the child's body was found.
Also, no pictures were allowed of the couple's attorneys who were in the room during the press conference, according to an editor at a local television station.
Chris Lopez, assistant city editor at The Denver Post, said the newspaper would have preferred to have had no conditions, but "we did not have a problem with them."
John Ramsey said the couple had been anxious to meet with the media but he said the couple felt they had an obligation to talk to authorities before they talked to the press.

Both parents met separately with two detectives and a representative of the Boulder County District Attorney's office on Wednesday, the first time in four months they had a formal interview with police.
John Ramsey said at first they were shocked and then outraged to be considered suspects in the crime.

"Then we understood statistically that is the sad state of affairs. We accepted being suspects. But what concerned us and still does is that any time spent looking at us (by police) is time that's wasted," he said.
The couple asked for the public's help in finding the killer of their 6-year-old daughter. Soon after the murder, the Ramseys put up a $100,000 reward for information leading to the killer.
"This ad with her most recent kindergarten picture will be appearing more frequently," said Patricia Ramsey, displaying an ad of JonBenet.

"We feel there are at least two people on the face of this earth who know who did it," she said, referring to the murderer and at least one confidant of the killer," she said without elaborating. "Please, please if you know anything, I beg you to call us," she said.
John Ramsey said an arrest is "absolutely necessary" for closure and looking for the killer would be "the sole mission for the rest of my life."
